task.description: Gate review on commit 4efff094 (branch feature/WF03-ISS0732-20260921), which adds a new precondition (verify_rehearsed/2) to Letflow.Definitions.Promotion.apply_review/4's with-chain, requiring a passing PromotionAssertionRun for the current plan_digest before a promotion can be released. Check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8. This touches a tenant-data write path (definition-promotion Apply), so this gate is mandatory before REVIEWER. Specifically verify: (1) verify_rehearsed/2's tenant-scoping is correct (queries the assertion run under the same prefix/tenant context as the rest of apply_review/4, no cross-tenant leak), (2) the new error reasons/HTTP responses do not leak internal state (e.g. another tenant's assertion-run details) in their messages, (3) the existing R8 assertions_failed==0 gate and verify_apply_digest/2's constant-time comparison are genuinely untouched (diff-confirm, not just trust the handoff's claim), (4) no new attacker-controlled input reaches a query/comparison without validation.
acceptance_criteria: PASS or FAIL verdict with specific findings against INV-1..INV-8
Confirms tenant-scoping of the new assertion-run lookup by reading the actual diff, not the design doc alone
Confirms R8/verify_apply_digest/2 are byte-for-byte untouched by diffing against origin/main
If FAIL: precise, actionable findings for ELIXIR-DEV rework (do not fix it yourself)

result.summary: Reviewed commit 4efff094 (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex, lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex) and the test-fixture follow-up commit against origin/main via `git diff origin/main...HEAD`. INV-1..INV-8 assessed individually below; no BLOCKER found. verify_rehearsed/2's lookup reuses the pre-existing, prefix-scoped Letflow.Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run/2 (definitions.ex untouched by this diff -- confirmed via `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions.ex` returning empty), so no new query bypasses tenant scoping. verify_apply_digest/2 and R8's assertions_failed==0 gate (promotions.ex run-assertions handler) are confirmed byte-for-byte untouched -- neither function appears in either diff hunk; only new type-union members, a doc-comment renumber, one new `with` clause, and one new private function were added to promotion.ex, and only three new render_apply/2 clauses were added to promotions.ex (inserted between the existing :invalid_transition and {:promotion_failed, :forbidden} clauses, none of the surrounding clauses modified).
issues: INV-1 (Tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES. verify_rehearsed/2 (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex:625-641, new) calls Letflow.Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run(review.id, opts), an existing, unmodified function (lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1179-1197) that scopes its Repo.one/2 call via `prefix: Keyword.fetch!(opts, :prefix)` -- the same :prefix mechanism 0003 mandates, and the same `opts` value already threaded through apply_review/4's other calls (get_review/2, and now this). No new query bypasses :prefix. (b) no migration in this diff. (c) no tenant_id field involved -- PromotionAssertionRun rows are looked up by review_id within the already-resolved prefix, not by a caller-supplied tenant identifier. Verdict: SATISFIED.

INV-2 (Server-side field authorisation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. Reference states 'no multi-tenant API surface exists (S4 not started)'; independently, the three new render_apply/2 clauses (lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex:632-652) each emit a single fixed detail string via Response.conflict/2 with no assertion-run fields (no run id, no digest value, no timestamps, no other tenant's identifiers) serialised into the body -- confirmed by reading the literal strings in the diff.
INV-3 (Untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No Lua/WASM path touched.
INV-4 (Secrets by reference only) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No secret material in this diff; confirmed no new config/env/token handling.

INV-5 (Not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. Reference states S4 not started; independently, get_latest_assertion_run/2's prefix-scoped lookup can only ever see rows in the caller's own resolved tenant schema (schema-per-tenant physically isolates other tenants' rows), so there is no cross-tenant 'exists but not yours' branch for this lookup to distinguish in the first place.
INV-6 (New data-access path proves its scoping) -- APPLIES and is SATISFIED by this handoff itself: PASS status, INV-1..INV-8 individually assessed above.

INV-7 (No SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES. `grep -n Repo.query lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex` -- no hits in either changed file; verify_rehearsed/2 goes through the existing Ecto.Query-based get_latest_assertion_run/2, no raw SQL introduced.

INV-8 (No unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES. verify_rehearsed/2's `case` on get_latest_assertion_run/2's result has an explicit clause for both {:error, :not_found} and {:ok, assertion_run} -- no bare match, no missing branch. plan_digest and assertion_run.plan_digest are compared only via PromotionDigest.verify_digest/2 (already-audited constant-time comparator used elsewhere in this same module for the same reason, per design §2.1 step 2) -- not a raw `==` that could behave unexpectedly, and not a new call to that function's own internals. `grep -n '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex` produces no new hits introduced by this diff.
INV-9 (SSRF/outbound URL validation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No outbound HTTP request added.

NON-BLOCKING, routed to REVIEWER not SECURITY-REVIEWER: design doc OQ-2 (lib/letflow/design/iss0732-promotion-apply-assertion-gate.md:315-333) correctly flags that get_latest_assertion_run/2 has no `status` filter, so a concurrent in-flight run (status: :running, assertions_failed defaults to 0 per insert_changeset/2) could satisfy verify_rehearsed/2's gate if it happens to be the most recent row for that review_id at read time. This is a same-tenant race/business-logic correctness question (does a not-yet-completed rehearsal wrongly count as passing), not a tenant-isolation, secret-leakage, SQL-injection, or unhandled-crash defect -- none of INV-1..INV-9 covers it, so it is not a SECURITY-REVIEWER BLOCKER. Flagging for REVIEWER to decide whether it warrants a follow-up (e.g. requiring status not in [:running] in addition to assertions_failed == 0) before or after this ships, per the design doc's own request.
